data.body:
CLOSE GATE REFUSED, correctly, and the fix went into the CODE rather than the criterion.

The completion verifier found that AC5 specifies the headroom bound 'at `< 800`' while the shipped assertion read `assert loc <= _HARD_CAP`. A file at EXACTLY 800 would have passed the implemented check and violated the stated criterion — a weaker guard than the plan promised. That is a real discrepancy, not pedantry, and it is the second time on this ticket that a gate caught something I asserted rather than checked.

TWO WAYS TO RESOLVE IT, and only one is legitimate. Weakening AC5 to `<= 800` would have matched the criterion to the code — the fix-the-test-to-match-the-implementation antipattern, and in a ticket whose entire subject is guards that cannot detect their own defect. Strengthened the CODE instead.

THE STRICT FORM IS ALSO THE BETTER SEMANTIC, so this is not mere compliance. The CI module-size gate fails only at 801, so `<= 800` does mirror CI — but 'passes CI' is a weaker property than 'has headroom', which is what a seam guard exists to assert. THREE files in this repo sit at EXACTLY 800 right now (plan_review/passes.py, plan_review/attest.py, _engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py), meaning the next one-line change to any of them is unlandable. ADR 0056 names this condition directly: a hot file 'must stop sitting ON the 800 gate, not merely pass it'. A guard that permits sitting on the cap permits exactly the state the epic exists to prevent.

Now `assert loc < _HARD_CAP`, with the reasoning and the three at-cap files cited inline so the next reader does not relax it back. Measured after the change: workflow_ops.py 794, config.py 793 — both comfortably under, so the strict form is not fragile on arrival. 3 passed, lint clean.

COST, stated plainly: amending forced patchset 2 on Gerrit change 1156, which drops the LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 it had already earned and requires both bots to re-run. That is the honest price of fixing the code instead of the criterion, and it is worth paying.
